subject.title: fix(secrets): keep startup alive when TTS SecretRefs are missing

question: Should a missing built-in TTS API-key SecretRef be treated as a cold-start-localized optional capability instead of preserving the current global fail-fast SecretRef contract?
rationale: Both behaviors are defensible: the patch prevents an optional speech credential from taking down the Gateway, but it deliberately changes when operators discover invalid active configuration and introduces a narrow exception inside a security-sensitive shared resolver.

options.title: Sponsor the narrow exception
options.body: Accept missing-value-only degradation during true cold startup, require exact-head live proof, and keep every other activation and error class fail-closed.

options.title: Preserve strict startup
options.body: Retain the existing fail-fast contract and close the PR, requiring operators to remove or restore the configured TTS SecretRef before startup.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the narrow exception
recommendation.body: Accept missing-value-only degradation during true cold startup, require exact-head live proof, and keep every other activation and error class fail-closed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the product-level startup contract established by foundational secrets-runtime work, and this person appears in the merger/reviewer history for that boundary.
